text:
Reproducibility requires controlling random streams and execution settings. PyTorch documents explicit DataLoader generators, worker seeding, and limits across software versions/platforms ([documentation](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/notes/randomness.md)). For this benchmark, retain preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42; isolate shuffle, training-negative, evaluation, and bootstrap generators so diagnostics cannot perturb training. Initialize model/dropout randomness reproducibly; architecture changes can consume different random draws, so identical seeds do not guarantee matched stochastic trajectories. Record configurations, versions, checkpoint selection, and RNG states. These are practical implications of the reproducibility guidance.

Sampled recommendation metrics can reverse full-catalog model rankings, even in expectation ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Preserve the pinned 99-negative protocol and describe results specifically as sampled HR@10. A suitable adaptation of [paired bootstrap resampling](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/) is to resample validation users within each category, using identical sampled user indices for both models; recompute category hit-rate differences and their equal-weight macro-average. Report a 95% interval conditional on the fixed models and candidate sets: it excludes training-seed and candidate-sampling uncertainty. One training seed cannot establish robustness across training randomness. Repeated checkpoint/configuration selection can overfit validation scores ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)); bootstrap intervals do not remove that bias. Under the limited budget, prioritize prespecified ablations, retain per-user hits and all trial results, and reserve held-out evaluation for the selected model.
